text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - Bund futures were steady in late trade after spending much of the day trading in positive territory thanks to strong overnight Treasuries. The September Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.20, down 0.07 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts managed to outperform struggling Bunds, but at 190 basis points, the 10-year spread over their German counterparts remained too wide. Gilt futures bounced back to life in late morning trade after the market reassessed the Confederation of British Industry's October distributive trades survey, released overnight. The September long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 109 up 14/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures drifted lower as weakness in the U.S. bond market prompted local traders to unwind positions ahead of a long weekend in France. The bond future started the day in a relatively positive mood but few traders had expected it to make any independent moves and overseas markets provided the direction. The September bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 127.20, down 0.08. from Thursday's settlement price.
ITALY - Italian bonds and futures ended firmer but off day's highs seen early in the sesssion as positive sentiment returned to the market, Traders said they had seen little Btp selling.
"With prices near highs we might have expected some significant profit-taking but sellers have been very thin on the ground," one said.
The September bond future on LIFFE was trading at 125.78 up 0.32 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries opened lower in quiet early morning trade as a mild profit-taking bout which began overseas spilled over into New York trading. The September Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 113-26/32, down 15/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.53 percent.

JAPAN - The key December Japanese government bond (JGB) futures contract ended Friday's Tokyo session sharply down as a correction continued. After hitting an all-time intraday high for any benchmark contract of 126.52 on Wednesday morning, the December has experienced a sharp downturn, plunging for the third straight session.
In after hours trading the June future on LIFFE was trading at 123.96, down 0.86 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
EUROBONDS - LONDON - The primary market got off to a slow start on Friday, with new issues seen in the dollar, mark, sterling and Swiss franc sectors.

Woolwich Building Society launched a 150 million stg perpetual bond via joint lead managers C.S. First Boston and HSBC Markets. It will be priced to yield 125 basis points over the 8.0 percent gilt due 2021.
